card.name: Joints inside management instructions after conditions
card.fires_on: Commas, 'be' and 'and' that come right after a drug or condition clause, just before an instruction on what to do next (reduce, prescribe, monitor, try another drug).

modes.label: Comma after if-clause
modes.description: A comma ending an 'if' or 'after' clause about a drug or condition, before the action to take.
modes.example: If an opioid analgesic is initiated in a patient already taking a benzodiazepine or other CNS depressant<<,>> prescribe a lower initial dose of the opioid

modes.label: 'be' after should/may
modes.description: The word 'be' after 'should' or 'may' in a statement about treatment or alternatives.
modes.example: Treatment should<< be>> supportive with appropriate monitoring.

modes.label: 'and' joining actions
modes.description: 'and' joining two instructions after a drug name.
modes.example: consider decreasing the dose of repaglinide<< and>> perform careful monitoring of blood glucose levels.

card.plain: It fires at the small joining words in a sentence where a drug situation is described and an instruction is about to follow.
